_what: Model-axis probe adjudication per the rule pre-registered at the pre-registered probe rule (see METHOD.md). For each stage-0 cluster, each probe arm's stance vs the fable-modal design: aligned | fork | unaddressed (fork = different interface/signal/shape, or >=2x on a constant). Probe claims quoted per verdict. new_cluster entries are design questions no fable arm raised. Adjudicator caveats are carried inline in 'note' fields rather than smoothed away; two calls materially affect the criterial count and are flagged: one borderline fork (t2/c5) and one correlated fork pair (t3/c1+c2 sharing a single root design choice).

t1-reveal.question: How is reveal performed?
t1-reveal.justification: opus d1: ShowItems, 'the one contract... all export'; gdbus->dbus-send->xdg-open containing dir. sonnet d1: ShowItems via dbus-send, fallback parent dir via open_with_system. Same interface, same chain shape as fable; leg count/order incidental as in stage 0.

t1-reveal.question: Where does the reveal errand execute?
t1-reveal.justification: opus d2: detached std::thread 'because deciding whether to try the next leg means waiting'. sonnet d2: std::thread::spawn over cx.background_executor(), matching the file's idiom.

t1-reveal.question: Which file:// authorities count as local?
t1-reveal.justification: opus d4: non-empty non-localhost refused as remote share. sonnet d4: empty or localhost only.

t1-reveal.question: Malformed %-escapes?
t1-reveal.justification: Neither probe declaration states a malformed-escape policy.

t1-reveal.question: Non-UTF-8 bytes in a decoded path?
t1-reveal.justification: Stage-0 fork cluster; neither probe arm declares a stance.

t1-reveal.question: query/fragment on a printed file:// URI?
t1-reveal.justification: Stage-0 fork cluster; neither probe arm declares a stance.

t1-reveal.question: Outgoing URI percent-encoding alphabet?
t1-reveal.justification: opus d3: encode before argv so no space/quote/backslash reaches the GVariant literal. sonnet d5+d8: hand-rolled, comma escaped for dbus-send array grammar, argv-never-shell. Same design; d8's argv rationale is complementary emphasis.

t1-reveal.question: How is the reveal target classified and gated?
t1-reveal.justification: opus d4: pure link_local_path over link_under output, one None gating both call sites. sonnet d6+d7: classify_link_under shared pipeline, reveal_under existence-gated, menu conditional.

t1-reveal.question: Chord placement and fall-through?
t1-reveal.justification: opus d5 and sonnet d3: Super+Ctrl before the open chord because Ctrl is contained; non-revealable falls through to open.

t1-reveal.question: Localise the context-menu row?
t1-reveal.justification: opus d6: hardcoded English like Copy/Paste siblings. sonnet d7: hardcoded row, no localisation plumbing (pane.rs is its only touched file).

t1-reveal.question: Help-modal discoverability?
t1-reveal.justification: opus d7: LINKS row, two keys, nine languages — the fable-unanimous move. sonnet: no discoverability claim and no lang.rs change; an omission, not a declared counter-decision.

t1-reveal.question: Changelog entry?
t1-reveal.justification: opus d8: Unreleased/Added entry plus info.html kiosk bullet. sonnet: none declared.

t2-adoption.question: What rule demotes a trivial session?
t2-adoption.justification: Fable-modal = handicapped save time (2 of 3). opus d2: four keys with a coarse recency bucket then an arranged-vs-throwaway TIER — the tier shape (fable-b's minority design), fork vs modal. sonnet d3: bounded recency HANDICAP of 30 minutes — modal shape but a constant 144x below the fable handicaps, fork on the constant. The two probe arms also disagree with each other, so no blind-spot signature.

t2-adoption.question: The demotion constant
t2-adoption.justification: Fable constants {72h, 7d, 7d}; modal 7d. opus d4: RECENT_WORK 7 days — aligned. sonnet d3: TRIVIAL_HANDICAP 30 minutes — two orders of magnitude below every fable constant; fork.

t2-adoption.question: What counts as trivial?
t2-adoption.justification: opus d3 and sonnet d2: panes <= 1, exactly the fable-unanimous boundary.

t2-adoption.question: How is substance recorded?
t2-adoption.justification: opus d1 and sonnet d1: top-level panes: Option<usize> written every save from the existing pane_count().

t2-adoption.question: How is the count read on scan?
t2-adoption.note: BORDERLINE, flagged: the criterial count is sensitive to this call. Opus stays in the hand-rolled-scanner family; the fork is the read structure itself.
t2-adoption.justification: Fable-modal: extend the hand-rolled stop-at-first-table scanner off the single whole-file read_to_string the scan already does. opus d5: replaces the whole-file read with a NEW bounded 4 KiB read_head and scans that head — a different read/control structure with observably different I/O ('never touches the tab tree even on a thirty-pane session', its own words), behaviourally divergent for any top-level key past 4 KiB. Fork by the rubric's letter; borderline because for well-formed files pinned by opus's own serialization test the semantics coincide. sonnet d6: one whole-body read serving both keys, mirrored scanner — aligned.

t2-adoption.question: Unknown pane count ranks as?
t2-adoption.justification: opus d3: absent count lands in the upper tier for free. sonnet d4: absent is 'unknown', never 'small', never handicapped.

t2-adoption.question: Workspace-hint precedence?
t2-adoption.justification: opus d2 key 1 untouched; sonnet d5: hint tier untouched and first, 'however small' honoured literally.

t2-adoption.question: Does the scratch-window theme borrow share the rank?
t2-adoption.justification: Fable-unanimous and fable-consensus cluster; neither probe arm mentions theme borrowing at all.

t2-adoption.question: How is the writer/scanner coupling verified?
t2-adoption.justification: opus d8: pins panes=31 ahead of the first [table] header by test. sonnet: names the assumption in not_done as 'inferred, not executed' and ships no pin test — a gap it declares, not a counter-decision.

t3-bell.question: What does a BEL become?
t3-bell.note: CORRELATED with c2, flagged: both sonnet forks share one root — the stateless gate has no held claim, therefore nothing to hold through an idle debounce.
t3-bell.justification: Fable-unanimous: the BEL parks/arms/defers as a claim and a later adjudication announces. opus d1: bell_verdict Ring|Hold|Drop with a held state — aligned. sonnet d1+d4: a gate AT ARRIVAL — 'either guard failing drops the bell event outright (no latch, no deferred marker, no state mutation)'; pass rings immediately, fail hands the finish entirely to the scan. Gate-and-drop is a different control structure from defer-and-resolve, with materially different behaviour: the bell's speed advantage is lost whenever the gate fails. Fork.

t3-bell.question: Working-agent suppression and the idle hold (bug 1)
t3-bell.justification: Fable-unanimous: live-screen thinking probe plus ring only after the same 300ms idle hold the scan uses. opus d3: held bell rings past the 300ms debounce, skipping the real-spell test — aligned. sonnet: agent_is_thinking probe aligned on the suppress half, but a passing bell rings IMMEDIATELY with no idle hold — the hold fable-b called 'what stops a beep landing in a redraw flicker from ringing' is absent. Fork.

t3-bell.question: How long does a parked claim survive continued work?
t3-bell.justification: Stage-0 fork cluster (void-at-next-tick / 10s / 5s). opus: a held bell has NO expiry — deadline rejected as a false-fire risk during long scrollback — a fourth distinct lifetime design; fork. sonnet: no parked state exists, so the question does not arise; unaddressed.

t3-bell.question: Restore-burst suppression signal (bug 2)
t3-bell.justification: Stage-0 three-way fork (typed-input gate / 30s observation clock / 10s spawn grace + evidence). opus d4+d5: a per-pane replay LATCH seeded from restore.resume, cleared by first keystroke or mouse-down via attend(), explicitly not a timer — a FOURTH distinct design. sonnet d1+d3: 2-second startup grace TIMER — fable-c's shape at a 5x smaller constant, and precisely the design opus d4 argues is 'defeated by a long transcript'. A FIFTH configuration. The probe arms disagree with each other, so no signature.

t3-bell.question: A repeat BEL while a finish is latched?
t3-bell.justification: opus d6: drops instead of re-announcing, matching the fable-unanimous choice and the scan arm's !bell guard. sonnet: gate does not consult the latch and no stance is declared.

t3-bell.question: How is the scan path kept unchanged?
t3-bell.justification: opus d3: 'the scan's own real path is bit-for-bit unchanged'. sonnet d5: scan and all three guards untouched.

t3-bell.question: Where does the decision logic live and how is it tested?
t3-bell.justification: opus d7: pure bell_verdict/announce_on_stop with truth-table tests in the existing idiom. sonnet d7: pure gate, three tests, live-PTY wiring declared unverified rather than faked.

t3-bell.question: Do the docs and changelog record the behaviour change?
t3-bell.justification: New question no fable arm raised. opus d8: Unreleased Fixed entry plus a 'A bell is a hint, not a finish' section in BELL_SOUNDS.md, 'the only written statement of the old contract'. sonnet d6: deliberately NO changelog entry, citing the two most recent commits in this feature area as precedent. Opposite declared decisions on one question: fork (non-criterial: presentation, and not a stage-0 cluster).

new_clusters_uncontested.question: How is time made testable in rank()?
new_clusters_uncontested.justification: opus d6: rank/rank_at(.., now) split per the file's _at/_in convention. No other arm in either stage addressed clock injection.

new_clusters_uncontested.question: Changelog entry for the adoption fix?
new_clusters_uncontested.justification: opus d9 adds one; no fable t2 arm and not sonnet declared any.
